title: Gorse the Brave Bridge-Tester
markdown:
Once upon a time, dawn burst over Craggy Peak! Brilliant colours painted the sky. Birds popped like tiny drums. Dewdrops sparkled. The air hummed with the Great Harvest Fair, pies and games and a whole village buzzing on the far side of the gorge.

Every day Gorse the goat dashed across the plank bridge for shiny pebbles. Tap-tap-tap went his hooves. The wood always argued. Wobble, creak, shiver. He loved the pebbles. He did not love the wobble. Can you imagine a goat who could leap a boulder and still freeze at a plank?

Until one day a storm struck! Wind kicked the peak. Rain drummed the boards. Crack! The bridge snapped in two. Gorse stared. The village sat cut off. The fair, with its pies and bouncy games, waited like a party behind glass.

Because of that, Gorse’s heart thumped a wild beat. He remembered Maple, the brilliant mole engineer. He zoomed down the muddy path, kicked gravel, burst into her workshop. Pegs. Ropes. The smell of wet wood and breakfast toast.

“Maple! The bridge is broken. The fair is ruined!”

Maple adjusted her spectacles. “A catastrophe. Not impossible!” She unrolled a giant blueprint that flapped like a flag. “Strong wood. Super ropes. And one brave tester.”

Gorse gulped. Testing meant wobble. But the fair. His friends. Apple pies. “I can help!”

“Fantastic!” Maple beamed. “Your springy legs will be perfect. Chief plank-tester.”

Because of that, work began. Maple’s team hammered and tied. Pegs bit the rock. Ropes sang when pulled tight. Gorse watched, hooves tapping, cool morning air in his nose. Then it was his turn. Maple held out a fresh plank. “Give it a go. Be brave.”

He pictured apple pies and bouncy castles. One hoof down. Wobble. The plank creaked. A shiver shot up his legs. He almost bolted back to toast and pebbles. Then he saw Maple’s determined face and the villagers’ hopeful eyes.

“You can do it, Gorse!”

With a mighty push he sprang. Bounce! Hooves landed. The plank held. Again. And again. Each test shrank the tremble. His hooves felt steadier. His heart beat an excited adventurous beat. He was a bridge-tester.

Because of that, they saved the wobbliest job for last. The final plank looked like a dare. Wind tugged it. It clapped against the ropes. Gorse took a brave breath. Thump-thump-thump. Wind whipped past his ears, a wild song. This was the leap that would open the fair or leave the pies on the wrong side of the gap.

Until finally he chose the jump. One giant springy leap! He landed firm. The plank held. The whole bridge held.

“It’s safe!” he called, voice booming across the gap that was no longer a gap. “The bridge is ready for the fair.”

Villagers cheered. Maple patted his back. “Brilliant, Gorse! Truly brave. You saved the fair.”

Ever since then, dawn over Craggy Peak still burst with colour, and Gorse still dashed for pebbles. Only now he dashed as the goat who tested the boards. He bounded onto the first plank, pies waiting, games bouncing, the day already spectacular. What do you think happened next? He grinned, kicked a shiny pebble, and raced toward whatever the morning asked him to try!
